item.title: The uncertainty operator, the Weil ground state and the zeros of zeta: a numerical study and conditional positivity of the Weil quadratic form
item.description: arXiv:2611.13129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Applying the Dirichlet principle to the Weil quadratic form $QW_\lambda$ on $L^2([\lambda^{-1},\lambda],d^*u)$--using only the primes $p\le\lambda^2$ of the Euler product--yields canonical finite-dimensional Hermitian matrices whose ground state has a Mellin transform with zeros proved real in full generality when the lowest eigenvalue is simple and even. While $\lambda^2=13$ gave $50$ zeros of $\zeta$, $\lambda^2=250$ ($\lambda\sim16$) gives the first $1000$ zeros with $>500$ correct decimals (the first with $1341$). We explain this via a correspondence between $QW_\lambda$ and Slepian's time-frequency uncertainty operator $U_\lambda=2-P_\lambda-\widehat P_\lambda$, diagonalized by prolate wave functions with eigenvalues $\delta_n(\lambda)\sim c_n\lambda^{2n+1}e^{-4\pi\lambda^2}$ (Fuchs). Via $\mathcal{E}(f)(u)=u^{1/2}\sum_{n\ge1}f(nu)$ and Gevrey smoothing, $\epsilon_\lambda\le C\delta_4(\lambda)(\log\lambda)^3$ is a theorem (Connes-Kastoris). Computations up to $\lambda^2=300$ ($\epsilon_\lambda(1)\sim10^{-1618}$) show a striking logarithmic coincidence with the Fuchs ladder, confirming this simplicity and evenness. Prolate vectors reproduce all minuscule eigenvectors, and conditioning by them and the pole term removes the minuscule spectrum: $QW_\lambda$ is a direct sum of a finite-dimensional near-radical part (Fuchs ladder) and an infinite-dimensional positive part from the Sonin space ($U_\lambda=2$). Under this ladder hypothesis and $QW_\lambda\ge0$, we bound the ground-state distance to the target with Mellin transform $\frac14\xi(s+\frac12)$ (Hurwitz' theorem). Finally, the semilocal trace formula gives the uncertainty principle via Coburn's lemma and proves, under a hypothesis valid at $\infty$, that $QW_\lambda\ge c>0$ outside a finite-dimensional near-self-dual space, reducing Weil positivity to a Schur complement at the ladder's edge.
item.dc:creator: Ronnie Andrews, Alain Connes, Antonio La Gatta

item.title: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ is $12$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the $\mathbb F_5$-gonality and the $\mathbb Q$-gonality of the modular curve $X_1(42)$ are both $12$, improving the previous lower bound of $10$. Since $J_1(42)(\mathbb Q)$ is finite, it follows that $12$ is the least degree in which $X_1(42)$ has infinitely many points. The lower bound comes from an exhaustive search over Riemann--Roch spaces, following Derickx and van Hoeij, using a new reduction by the orbits of a cyclic group of automorphisms of order $12$ on places of degree at most $5$ ($743\,231$ Riemann--Roch spaces). An earlier search with the reductions from van Hoeij's code (about $3$ million Riemann--Roch spaces, about $6$ times more CPU time) gives the same result and serves as supporting evidence. We prove the reductions and record the data needed to reproduce the computations.
item.dc:creator: Sourajyoti Maiti

item.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
item.description: arXiv:2611.13459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-\delta_k+o(1)})$ where $\delta_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.
item.dc:creator: Eilidh McKemmie

item.title: A counterexample to the Erd\H{o}s--Mahler conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.13604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We disprove a 1939 conjecture of Erd\H{o}s and Mahler by constructing, for every real $\tau\ge4$, a Cantor set of numbers of irrationality exponent $\tau$, each having infinitely many regular continued-fraction convergents of the form $2^a/3^b$.
item.dc:creator: Diego Marques

item.title: A Threshold-Crossing Condition for the Least Colossally Abundant Counterexample to Robin's Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.13606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the constraints that a hypothetical least Colossally Abundant (CA) counterexample to Robin's Inequality would place on the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$. In the single-prime case we express the least CA counterexample $N$ as $M\cdot p$, where $M$ is its CA predecessor and $p$ is prime. Using the von Mangoldt explicit formula for $\psi(x)$, we express $\ln p$ in terms of a sum over the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$ and split that expression into its baseline contribution $\mathcal{R}_0(p)$ and its off-line distortion. When both converge, we show that the off-line distortion is negative whenever $1+1/(e^{\mathcal{R}_0(p)}+e^{2\mathcal{R}_0(p)}+\cdots+e^{(v+1)\mathcal{R}_0(p)})\le\ln(\ln M+\mathcal{R}_0(p))/\ln\ln M$, where $v$ is the $p$-adic valuation of $M$. In the case where the least CA counterexample is the product of its CA predecessor and two primes (the semiprime case), the logarithm of the product of the two primes is the sum of two von Mangoldt expansions. An analogous inequality implies that at least one of the off-line distortions of the two expansions is negative.
item.dc:creator: Bruce Zimov

item.title: On the equidistribution of eigenfunctions of higher dimensional cat maps modulo prime powers
item.description: arXiv:2611.13720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The so-called $\mathit{Cat\ Map}$, which is a linear map generated by symplectic matrices $A \in \operatorname{Sp}(2d,\mathbb Z)$ modulo an integer $N\ge 1$ is a classical discrete model of quantum ergodicity. For $d=1$ it has been investigated by P. Kurlberg and Z. Rudnick (2001), J. Bourgain (2007) and A. Ostafe, I. E. Shparlinski and J. F. Voloch (2023). The significantly more difficult case of $d>1$ has been studied by P. Kurlberg, A. Ostafe, Z. Rudnick and I. E. Shparlinski (2025). All these works apply only to almost all $N$ and are unable to provide an explicit sequence of such ``good'' values of $N$. The authors (2026) have given such a construction with a polynomial decay on the corresponding matrix coefficients. Here we use some new ideas and improve this bound.
item.dc:creator: Subham Bhakta, Igor E. Shparlinski

item.title: Periods and CM motives of abelian type
item.description: arXiv:2611.13723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We associate algebraic Hecke characters to certain invertible motives for absolute Hodge cycles with coefficients in a number field $K$, reversing a viewpoint of Schappacher. These motives $N$ include abelian motives and a new notion of algebraic motive. This Hecke character determines the complex and the $p$-adic periods of $N$, and is determined by the latter; this gives a proof of the Mumford-Tate conjecture for $N$. When $K$ and $N$ are abelian, we prove a refinement of the Gross-Deligne conjecture, as well as $l$-adic and $p$-adic variants. We also formulate a version of the algebraic relations between rational values of the gamma function given by Koblitz and Ogus in terms of a distribution with values in the Picard group of the category of (abelian) Chow motives.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Kahn, Noriyuki Otsubo

item.title: Diophantine approximation with prime denominators in short intervals
item.description: arXiv:2611.13767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any real number $x$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer, and let $\alpha$ be any irrational number. We prove that, for $Y=X^\gamma$ with $7/12<\gamma\le 1$ and $0<\theta<\min \{(12\gamma-7)/24, 1/9\}$, there exist infinitely many $X$ for which there are primes $p$ satisfying $$ \|\alpha p\|<p^{-\theta},\quad X-Y<p<X. $$ Moreover, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of such primes. Our result extends the admissible range of short intervals in the corresponding result of Baier and Roy from $2/3<\gamma\le 1$ to $7/12<\gamma\le 1$, reaching Huxley's classical range for primes in short intervals and also improves the exponent $\theta$ in $2/3\le \gamma\le 3/4.$
item.dc:creator: Habibur Rahaman

item.title: A Moment Proof of the Hollman-Xiang Conjectures on Kloosterman Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.13848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F=\F_{2^n}$ and let \[ \mathcal T_1=\{t\in F:\Tr_{F/\F_2}(t)=1\}. \] For an integer $u=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_i2^i$ of even binary weight, put \[ L_u(X)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_iX^{2^i}, \qquad L_{1,u}(t)=t+L_u(t^{-1}). \] Hollmann and Xiang conjectured that $L_{1,u}$ permutes $\mathcal T_1$ if and only if $u\in\{0,3,6,10\}$. We prove the necessity by a moment method; the sufficiency is their Theorem~4.1. The quadratic moment yields a cyclic autocorrelation identity, while the cubic moment gives a two-variable group-algebra identity. An elimination argument reduces the coefficient word to a monomial or a complementary monomial, and explicit cubic and quartic moments complete the classification. We also prove Hollmann and Xiang's Conjecture~4.5. Namely, if $n>3$ and \[ L_{c,d}(x)=L_c(x)+L_d(x^{-1}) \] is a Kloosterman polynomial on $\F_{2^n}$, then its positive linearized part $L_c$ is injective on both trace fibers. This second result follows from relative quadratic and cubic moment identities and a spectral-zero rigidity argument. Consequently every Kloosterman polynomial is obtained by composing one of $L_{1,0},L_{1,3},L_{1,6},L_{1,10}$ with a linearized map that is injective on both trace fibers.
item.dc:creator: Yi Li

item.title: When do all iterates of $x^2 + a$ have maximal Galois group?
item.description: arXiv:2611.14014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide an (in our opinion) simpler proof of the main results of [Stoll1992,Li2020,Li2021] on the question for which integers $a$ the Galois groups of all iterates of $x^2 + a$ are maximal (equivalently, the associated arboreal Galois representation is surjective). At the same time, we extend the results to rational parameters $a$. The main result states that for a subset of rational numbers of relative density $1/2$ in the complement of a certain open interval, the maximality of the Galois group of the second iterate is sufficient for the arboreal Galois representation to be surjective. We also discuss experimental evidence suggesting that a similar statement involving the fourth iterate may hold in general. The results were obtained in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic's AI model); they are also formalized in Lean (except for the experimental evidence).
item.dc:creator: Michael Stoll

item.title: Explicit plane models for all Galois quotients of the Hermitian curve
item.description: arXiv:2611.14073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $H=k(x,y)$ be the Hermitian function field $y^q+y=x^{q+1}$ over $k=\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, and let $G$ be a subgroup of its $k$-automorphism group $\operatorname{PGU}(3,q)$. We give a uniform construction of a plane model for $H^G$. For each of $x$ and $y$, we multiply its distinct translates under the stabilizer $S$ in $G$ of their common pole, then sum the translates of that product over $G/S$. The two resulting functions $U,V$ generate $H^G$. In $H^G$, their only pole is the restriction of the common pole, with coprime orders $a=q/|G_x|$ and $b=(q+1)/|G_y|$, where $G_x,G_y$ are the subgroups of $G$ fixing $x,y$, respectively. Their plane equation has degree $\max(a,b)\leq q+1$ and can be recovered from finitely many Laurent coefficients of $U,V$ at the common pole of $x,y$. All steps are effective given matrix generators of $G$. The total delta invariant of this affine model is $g(H^{G_xG_y})-g(H^G)=\frac{1}{2}(a-1)(b-1)-g(H^G)$. Consequently $g(H^G)\leq\frac{1}{2}(a-1)(b-1)$; when $g(H^G)\geq2$, the model is smooth if and only if $G=G_xG_y$. The generator construction also applies to other function fields admitting two functions whose only pole is a common rational place, with coprime orders.
item.dc:creator: Liming Ma, Yipeng Wang

item.title: A generalized Vojta-R\'emond inequality over adelic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.14123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Dill's generalized Vojta-R\'emond inequality to proper adelic curves of characteristic zero, under an explicit Siegel hypothesis. The geometric case is closely related to recent work on Mordell-Lang plus geometric Bogomolov for semi-abelian varieties. Our formulation retains Dill's generality for products of distinct projective varieties. The appendix establishes the Siegel input for arithmetic function fields with nef and big polarizations on the model.
item.dc:creator: Ningjun Jiang

item.title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.14125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. We give an explicit lower bound for the asymptotic rate. The lower bound for the relative minimum distance follows from the Pieri formula on the space of flags in the Hodge bundle and an intersection argument along its strata. We also prove that, for $p\ge5$ and $0\le w\le p+1$, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists precisely of the multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant. For $g=2,3$, the geometry of the supersingular locus gives explicit bounds for the relative minimum distance and recovery sets whose sizes are bounded independently of the level.
item.dc:creator: Yota Maeda

item.title: Sun's conjecture on a certain ternary quadratic form
item.description: arXiv:2611.14161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an asymptotic form of Sun's conjecture concerning representations by the ternary quadratic polynomial \[ P(x,y,z)=x(5x+1)+\dfrac{y(5y+1)}{2}+\dfrac{z(5z+1)}{2}. \] More precisely, we prove that every sufficiently large integer is represented by $P$, with an effectively computable threshold. The proof begins by reducing the representation problem to that of a positive definite ternary quadratic form. We then study its genus and associated theta series, using explicit representation identities to determine the Shimura lift of the relevant weight-$3/2$ cusp form. Through Waldspurger's formula, this allows us to relate its Fourier coefficients to central values of quadratic twists of a weight-two modular form. Finally, effective lower bounds for class numbers, together with subconvexity estimates, show that the cuspidal contribution is dominated by the genus average for all sufficiently large integers, yielding the desired result.
item.dc:creator: Shilun Wang

item.title: A complete classification of permutation binomials of the form $X^r(X^{2(q-1)}+a)$ over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.14162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q$ be a prime power. We determine, for all positive integers $e$ and $r$, the coefficients $a\in\mathbb{F}_{q^e}$ for which $X^r(X^{2(q-1)}+a)$ permutes $\mathbb{F}_{q^e}$. For odd $q$ and $a\ne0$ there are no such permutations when $e\geqslant4$ is even. Over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, with $r$ unrestricted, the permutation binomials are characterized by congruence and coprimality conditions on $r$ and equations of degree at most two for $(-a)^{(q+1)/2}$, together with one sporadic family over $\mathbb{F}_{11^2}$; this gives an explicit form of Hou's finiteness theorem for each fixed odd $r>3$. The remaining cases follow from the known classification for the exponent difference $q-1$. In the quadratic case, power sums whose binomial expansions are sparse by Lucas' theorem determine the exponent one $p$-adic digit at a time. In even degree at least four, an exponent congruence reduces the problem to the existence of a collision, which we obtain by counting norm ratios on the projective line. A power substitution extends the classification to $X^r(X^{d(q-1)}+a)$ whenever $\gcd\bigl(d,(q^e-1)/(q-1)\bigr)=2$.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Tang, Xiang Fan

item.title: The exponent $3/4$ for the exceptional sets of the equations $K/n=1/x+1/y+1/z$
item.description: arXiv:2611.14167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $K\ge4$ let $E_K(N)$ be the number of integers $2\le n\le N$ for which $K/n=1/x+1/y+1/z$ has no solution in positive integers; $K=4$ is the Erd\H{o}s-Straus equation. We prove that $E_K(N)\le N\exp(-c((\log N)^3/K)^{1/4})$ with absolute constants $c,B>0$, uniformly for $4\le K\le(\log N)^3/B$. This improves the exponent $2/3$ of Vaughan's bound of 1970. The bound is non-trivial for $K$ up to a constant times $(\log N)^3$, which is, up to a factor $(\log\log N)^{2+o(1)}$, the scale at which, by work of Pomerance and Weingartner, exceptional primes become common. The sieve is combinatorial: a truncated inclusion-exclusion over the classes of parametric solutions, whose second moment is the partition function of a two-copy polymer gas, bounded by a real form of the Koteck\'y-Preiss criterion. Averaging over the residue classes of the small primes gives the family its full mass, and summing each cluster in a random order bounds the cluster sums. Since a divisor of an exception is an exception, nothing about the small primes themselves is needed, and the sieve can use the classes of the whole family of parametric solutions, one triple per class. All constants are explicit, and the whole proof has been checked in the proof assistant Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Dmytro Trybushnyi

item.title: A Complete Classification of Maximal Hyperelliptic Curves Related to Chebyshev Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.14198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\varphi_d$ be the Chebyshev polynomial with $\varphi_d(t+t^{-1})=t^d+t^{-d}$, and let $H_d$ be the hyperelliptic curve $y^2=\varphi_d(x)$. We determine all pairs $(d,p)$, with $p\nmid2d$ prime, for which $H_d$ is maximal over some finite field of characteristic $p$, together with all such fields. For $p\equiv1\pmod4$ only partial results were known. In this case, for odd $d$ we show that the Jacobian of $H_d$ is supersingular if and only if $H_d$ is maximal over a finite extension of $\mathbb{F}_p$, and that this happens precisely when $d=\ell^n$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod4$ prime and $p$ a generator of $(\mathbb{Z}/\ell^n\mathbb{Z})^\times$; we also compute the Frobenius polynomial. Necessity comes from the Shimura--Taniyama formula together with the non-vanishing of the value at $0$ of certain Dirichlet L-series and information about the action of Frobenius on $2$-torsion. The case of even $d$ and $p\equiv1\pmod 4$ follows from the odd case, by a short reduction.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Tafazolian, Jaap Top

item.title: Counting Rational Points on Cayley's Cubic Surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.14226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study rational points of bounded maximum-coordinate height on the split four-nodal Cayley cubic surface over \(\mathbb Q\), with its nine lines removed. Writing \(U\) for this open subset and \(N_U(B)\) for its counting function, we establish \[ N_U(B)\sim c_{\mathrm{Peyre}}B(\log B)^6. \] The argument starts from the universal-torsor parametrization and combines two counting methods over complementary ranges of the auxiliary variables. The two-dimensional lattice count is controlled by averages of reciprocal shortest-vector lengths and character-moment bounds, while Poisson summation treats the complementary parameter range. The main contribution is the uniform control needed to combine these methods when the size parameters of the auxiliary variables vary independently: the estimates retain every coprimality condition, the original height weight, and the full set of auxiliary tuples contributing to the geometric error. Divisibility estimates without an additional power of the height parameter control the sieve tail and justify removing the sieve after taking the height limit. We track the derivative losses and boundary contributions throughout the summation, and identify the common continuous main term with Peyre's constant by computing the effective-cone volume and the real and finite local densities.
item.dc:creator: Xiaodong Zhao

item.title: Divisor Folding and Finite-Group Trace Obstructions
item.description: arXiv:2611.14481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a symmetric integer frequency set of size $n$ with Fourier floor $K$, we study a positive trace weighted by the reciprocal of the regularized Fourier multiplier. If restriction to frequencies divisible by $p$ leaves $n/p+O(K^2)$ frequencies, then for $n\ge K^4$ and $p\ll n/K^3$ the original trace differs by $O(n)$ from $p$ times the core trace at the inherited regularization. The transfer reaches cores of size $\asymp K^3$ and preserves vanishing triple density with diverging normalized triple count. We construct exactly regular finite abelian spectra at these scales for which the linear core trace bound fails by a power. The examples use unions of classical semiprimitive cyclotomic classes and also give obstructions in both reflection parities in odd characteristic. Finally, we bound the overlap of lifts of a core by its smallest positive Fourier height and the symmetry of the lifts. These bounds exclude balanced lifts of the binary examples in a range of cyclic extensions and quantify the asymmetry required in odd prime split extensions.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Shankar

item.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
item.description: arXiv:2611.14486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $0<\gamma_1\leq \gamma_2\leq \cdots$ be the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros $\rho_n$ of the Riemann zeta function in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity. Selberg proved unconditionally that there exists $\lambda_0<1$ such that a positive proportion of the zeros $\rho_n$ satisfy $\gamma_{n+1}-\gamma_n\leq 2\pi \lambda_0/\log \gamma_n$. Simoni\v{c}, Trudgian and Turnage-Butterbaugh were the first to obtain an explicit value in Selberg's theorem, showing that $\lambda_0=1- 10^{-3\cdot 10^{13}}$ is admissible. This was considerably improved by Zhao who showed that $\lambda_0= 1-2.36\cdot 10^{-6}$ is admissible. In this paper, we use a different approach, based on an unconditional variant of Montgomery's pair correlation method, to obtain a substantial improvement of these results, showing unconditionally that $\lambda_0=0.7892<4/5$ is admissible.
item.dc:creator: Youness Lamzouri

item.title: Zeros of Katz's p-adic Eisenstein series E2
item.description: arXiv:2611.14502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every prime $p\geq5$, the zeros of Katz's $p$-adic Eisenstein series $E_2$ on elliptic curves with good ordinary reduction have exactly $\lfloor p/12\rfloor+1$ distinct $j$-invariants. We prove that all these invariants lie in finite unramified extensions of $\mathbf{Q}_p$. Their reductions are given by a classical formula involving the supersingular polynomial, and each nonelliptic residue class contains a unique simple zero. For the Legendre family, hypergeometric congruences determine the polynomial of the lifted invariants modulo every power of $p$. We also study isogenies between the zeros. Each $p$-power isogeny class contains at most one zero $j$-invariant, and any two distinct isogenous zero invariants are algebraic over $\mathbf{Q}$. At a fixed cyclic degree, the nonelliptic isogenies give points in a finite divisor over $\mathbf{Q}$ on the corresponding modular curve. Its degree bounds their number and their fields of definition, and excludes several small degrees. The only zeros with complex multiplication have $j=0$ or $1728$. Whether a non-CM zero can have an algebraic $j$-invariant remains open.
item.dc:creator: Abdellah Sebbar, Khalil Besrour

item.title: Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.13044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $h_q(n)$ be the largest codimension of a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ whose cyclic shifts cover the whole space. For $r>0$, we characterize the inequality $h_q(n)\ge r$ in terms of cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes over vector alphabets with covering radius one, no nonzero word of block weight one, and a scalar dual generated by the shifts of one word. For $k,m\ge2$, let $I_q(j)$ count the monic irreducible polynomials of degree $j$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. If $k$ is prime or $m\ge2\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}I_q(j)+2$, we prove that a cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$ linear perfect code of length $\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ exists if and only if $\gcd(m,q-1)=1$. When this condition holds, we also obtain \(h_q\!\left(\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}\right)=k(m-1).\) Restriction of scalars gives the same criterion for every $m\ge2$ when $q$ is odd, $q+1$ is a power of two, and $k=2p$ with $p$ prime. We also show that $h_q(q^k+1)=k$ exactly when $q$ is even, for every $k\ge1$.
item.dc:creator: Yangcheng Li, Pingzhi Yuan

item.title: A cyclotomic Artin-Tate formula and sphere packing for K3 surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.13468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give new necessary conditions on the Weil polynomial of a K3 surface over a finite field using techniques from the theory of sphere packing. By comparing the Artin-Tate formula over a finite extension, we derive a special values formula at roots of unity that involves the discriminant of the Frobenius coinvariant lattice. Known bounds on the minimum discriminants of even rootless lattices then imply nontrivial lower bounds on these special values. Applying these new conditions to Kedlaya and Sutherland's list of candidate Weil polynomials of K3 surfaces over the field with 2 elements rules out over 50% of the candidates.
item.dc:creator: Asher Auel, Sair Shaikh

item.title: Nonnegative weak tilings and the Coven-Meyerowitz condition (T2)
item.description: arXiv:2611.13593v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a general method, in finite cyclic groups, for constructing nonnegative rational functions $f$, normalized by $f(0)=1$, that satisfy the Coven-Meyerowitz condition $(T1)$ but fail $(T2)$, such that $f$ is a weak complement for a set tile $A$. Motivated by the unsupported-divisor questions in arXiv:2507.11672, we show that if a set tile $A$ admits an unsupported divisor, then a suitable dilation of $A$ admits such a rational weak complement $f$. Using this method, we construct an explicit example in the group $\mathbb{Z}_{180}$. The weak complements in our explicit perturbative constructions are not positive definite because of restrictions on the Fourier support of the perturbations. Thus these constructions do not resolve the proposed extension of the Coven-Meyerowitz conditions to positive-definite weak tilings (arXiv:2411.03854, Problem 1.2).
item.dc:creator: Gergely Kiss, Caleb Marshall, M\'at\'e Matolcsi, G\'abor Somlai

item.title: Non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory and stacks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the first half of these notes, we survey some aspects of the stack-theoretic perspective on $p$-adic Hodge theory, with an emphasis on the non-abelian aspects. In the second half, we report ongoing joint work on ``quantizing'' non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory.
item.dc:creator: Bhargav Bhatt

item.title: Davenport Constants of High-Dimensional Integer Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.14140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Davenport constant of a finite set of integer vectors is the maximum length of an irreducible zero-sum sequence over that set. For nonempty sets closed under negation, it equals the largest $\ell_1$-norm of a Graver basis element of the matrix formed by those vectors. We study extremal and average-case versions in growing dimension, with applications to integer programming. For integer cubes $[-R,R]^d \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^d$, totally unimodular encodings improve on the upper bounds from direct circuit decomposition, while random perturbations of Hadamard matrices give new lower bounds. A key ingredient is a uniform affine Bernoulli variant of Nguyen and Wood's surjectivity theorem. In every sufficiently large dimension the sign-cube lower bound is $d^{d/2}2^{-d-o(d)}$, and the integer-cube lower bound is $R^d d^{d/2}2^{-o(d)}$ uniformly for polynomially bounded integer radii. For random sign-cube sequences of even length conditioned on summing to zero, we prove a sharp threshold from irreducibility to reducibility at $d\log d/\log 4$, far below the extremal scale. For fixed $p$ and $R$, we determine exact exponential rates for lattice $\ell_p$-balls when $p=1$, $R\geq3$, or $2\leq p<\infty$, $\lfloor R^p\rfloor\geq3$. For each fixed integer $k\geq3$, we determine the exponential rate of the worst-case $\ell_1$-distance from an optimal LP vertex to the nearest integer optimum in standard-form programs with ternary matrices having at most $k$ nonzero entries per column.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Kuhlmann, Timm Oertel, Nicola Wengiel

item.title: Parabolic induction and pullback of perverse sheaves on Vogan varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.14156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a Levi subgroup of a quasisplit connected reductive group $G$ over a $p$-adic field. Vogan's geometric perspective on the local Langlands correspondence fixes a perfect pairing between the Grothendieck group of representations of $G$ and its pure inner forms with a fixed infinitesimal parameter and the Grothendieck group of equivariant perverse sheaves on the associated Vogan variety. Granting a list of desiderata for the enhanced local Langlands correspondence, we show that parabolic induction $\mathrm{Ind}_M^G$ is the transpose of geometric restriction $\xi^*$ with respect to this pairing if and only if the $p$-adic analogue of the Kazhdan--Lusztig hypothesis and the expected multiplicity formula for tempered induction both hold. The identity refines to one for each pure inner form of $G$.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Heng Lo, Mishty Ray

item.title: The zero-sum constant $\mathsf{s}_p^*$ and inverse problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.14248v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime. We denote by $\mathsf{s}_{p}^{*}$ the smallest integer $l$ such that, out of any given $l$ integers coprime with $p$, one can select $p$ integers satisfying that the sum of the $p$ integers is a multiple of $p$, but not a multiple of $p^{2}$. It was conjectured that $\mathsf{s}_p^*=2p+1$. In this paper we prove this conjecture and solve the corresponding inverse problem. More precisely, we characterize all sequences of $2p$ integers coprime to $p$ in which every $p$-term subsequence with sum a multiple of $p$ also has sum a multiple of $p^2$.
item.dc:creator: Cong Lin

item.title: Intermediate Growth and Rigidity in Primitive Circulant Spectral Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.14290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: At prime graph orders, the complete nontrivial and primitive Fourier spectra of a circulant coincide. We show that this agreement conceals a strong algebraic separation when the graph order varies. For any nonempty finite jump set $S$, let $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ be the algebra of arithmetic functions obtained by evaluating symmetric power sums on the primitive spectrum, filtered by power-sum weight. Removing the common Euler-totient term gives a reduced, locally finite algebra $B_S$, and we prove a filtration-preserving isomorphism $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}\cong B_S[T_2]$. Thus $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ is non-Noetherian and has Krull dimension one. Its filtered dimensions satisfy $\exp(c_S\sqrt{D/\log D})\leq \rho_S^{\mathrm{prim}}(D) \leq\exp(C_S\sqrt D)$ for large $D$, and its associated-graded Hilbert series is nonrational. Despite agreement on every prime order, the primitive and full spectral evaluation algebras intersect only in $\mathbb{Q}$. More strongly, no nonconstant primitive spectral function is eventually quasirational on residue classes. We give an exact finite-matrix rank formula and determine the quotient obtained by restricting to integers with large prime factors.
item.dc:creator: Juan D. V\'elez, Carlos A. Cadavid

item.title: Reconstructing Numerical Semigroups from Circulant Spectral Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.14316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The polynomial algebra generated by the spectral moments of a family of circulant graphs consists of all eventually polynomial sequences in the graph order; as an unfiltered algebra, it therefore carries little information about the jumps. We show that its natural power-sum weight filtration retains substantially finer arithmetic data. For a finite jump set $S$ with $\gcd(S)=1$ and $M=\max S$, the relevant invariant is the numerical semigroup $\Sigma_S=\langle M,M-s,M+s:s\in S\rangle$, which arises from the lengths of closed walks winding around the cycle. We prove that the eventual global filtered dimension is $MD+\lfloor D/2\rfloor+1-M(M+1)-g(\Sigma_S)$. Restricting graph orders to $n\equiv a\pmod q$, for $q\mid M$, replaces the genus term by the number of gaps of $\Sigma_S$ in the class $-a\pmod q$; the class $a=0$ gives the genus of the quotient semigroup $\Sigma_S/q$. These formulas yield an inverse reconstruction theorem: the unrestricted dimensions determine $M$, and the dimensions in all classes modulo $M$ at one common stable degree determine the Ap\'ery set and hence $\Sigma_S$. We give effective thresholds, exact examples, and a finite-rank algorithm valid in every degree. Reconstruction of the semigroup need not identify the original jump set.
item.dc:creator: Juan Diego Velez Caicedo, Carlos A. Cadavid

item.title: Ramification of torsion packets on curves with good-reduction Jacobians
item.description: arXiv:2611.14337v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p\ge5$ be a prime number, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Write $R=W(k)$ for the ring of Witt vectors over $k$, and $K$ for the field of fractions of $R$. Let $X$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over $K$ of genus greater than one. Write $J$ for the Jacobian variety of $X$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$ of $K$. In the present paper, we prove that if $J$ has good reduction over $R$, then every point $x\in X(\overline{K})$ such that $[\sigma x-x]$ is torsion for each $\sigma\in \operatorname{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ is $K$-rational.
item.dc:creator: Arata Minamide

item.title: Progression-free sets in class $2$ and arbitrary finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.14464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study progression-free sets in arbitrary finite groups. We transfer sharp upper bounds from abelian groups to nilpotent groups of class $2$, and from nilpotent groups to arbitrary groups. Combining a recent result of Raghavan with the author's theorem on large subgroups of class $2$ gives \[ r_3(G) \, \leq \, C \, |G|\exp\left( -c\frac{(\log|G|)^{1/6}}{(\log\log|G|)^{1/3}}\right) \] for every finite group as $|G|\to\infty$. This improves the estimates obtained by using the abelian subgroup supplied by Pyber's theorem.
item.dc:creator: Luca Sabatini

item.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
item.description: arXiv:2611.14468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. The same pair determines the principal eigenvalue whose sign governs persistence, so early prevalence can inform the threshold even when the individual rates remain uncertain. We prove global weak well-posedness and quantitative parameter stability for the SIS system and use the resulting observation-map estimates to establish Bayesian well-posedness. For an initial infection of size $\varepsilon$, we derive a uniform second-order expansion that describes how the separate rates enter prevalence. Incidence depends explicitly on transmission at leading order. When the noise standard deviation is proportional to $\varepsilon$, we prove $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence in Hellinger distance of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits for both prevalence alone and joint prevalence and incidence data. We bound the principal eigenvalue using the growth rate of the infected $L^2$ norm between two times. This rate gives a lower bound for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates spatial transients from nonlinear saturation. Uniform spectral estimates and bounds on infection size and measurement error give sufficient conditions for persistence and extinction. We also bound the error in posterior persistence probabilities under forward and eigenvalue approximation, accounting for posterior mass near the threshold. Numerical examples illustrate threshold inference and the predicted \(O(\varepsilon)\) convergence of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits in Hellinger distance.
item.dc:creator: Duc-Lam Duong

item.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
item.description: arXiv:2611.14517v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let C_h be the closure of the nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficients of modulus at most h. With the nonzero real roots included, the closure is connected at every height; without them, connectedness becomes arithmetic. We prove that C_h is connected exactly when h=q(q-1) is a pronic number 2, 6, 12, 20, ..., and has at least five components otherwise. At height two this confirms a twenty-year-old numerical observation of Shmerkin and Solomyak on double zeros of power series: apart from 1/2 they form the interval $[1/\rho,1)=C_2\cap(0,1)$, with $\rho$ the tribonacci constant. Disconnection is almost always infinite. For (p-1)^2<h<=p^2-3, $h\neq p(p-1)$, infinitely many components with nonempty interior accumulate at $\pm p$ and $\pm 1/p$, and when h<p(p-1) these four points are themselves components. Next to each square q^2>=16, at least two of the three heights q^2-2, q^2-1, q^2 have infinitely many components accumulating at a common point of (1/(q+1),1/q). Explicit series give infinitely many components at every nonpronic height below 167 other than 1, 3, 4, 9, 25, 63 and 81, and in general at most sqrt(X)+1 nonpronic heights h<=X can have finitely many components, although C_h is a Peano compactum at every height. The proofs compare values and derivatives of all admissible power series near a real double zero; the comparison sets are open and closed in the whole core, so components separated near the axis cannot reconnect elsewhere. On the real axis, the double zeros at heights 1, 3, 4, 7 form sets with infinitely many components; at height one this proves a conjecture of Shmerkin and Solomyak and one of Solomyak on the connectedness locus for pairs of affine maps.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Espigule

item.title: $2$-adic integral models of some Shimura varieties with parahoric level structure
item.description: arXiv:2301.12981v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct integral models over $p=2$ for some Shimura varieties of abelian type with parahoric level structure, extending the previous work of Kim-Madapusi, Kisin, Pappas, and Zhou. These integral models are canonical in the sense of Pappas-Rapoport.
item.dc:creator: Jie Yang

item.title: Heights of Drinfeld modular polynomials and Hecke images
item.description: arXiv:2410.11132v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain explicit upper and lower bounds on the size of the coefficients of the Drinfeld modular polynomials $\Phi_N$ for any monic $N\in\mathbb{F}_q[t]$. These polynomials vanish at pairs of $j$-invariants of Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$-modules of rank 2 linked by cyclic isogenies of degree $N$. The main term in both bounds is asymptotically optimal as $\mathrm{deg}(N)$ tends to infinity. We also obtain precise estimates on the Weil height and Taguchi height of Hecke images of Drinfeld modules of rank 2.
item.dc:creator: Florian Breuer, Fabien Pazuki, Zhenlin Ran

item.title: Class number of real quadratic fields of explicit discriminant
item.description: arXiv:2412.06351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the class numbers of a family of real quadratic fields $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ whose discriminants possess a specific exponential structure. More precisely, the discriminant $D$ is given by $(b(4bs+1)^k+s)^2 + (4bs+1)^k$, where $b$, $s$ and $k$ are positive integers, and $D$ is assumed to be square-free. This non-Richaud-Degert family is characterized by a predictable continued fraction expansion for $\sqrt{D}$, which allows for an explicit expression of its fundamental unit. When the parameters $b$ and $s$ are fixed, the corresponding regulators grow asymptotically like $(\log D)^2$. By analyzing the associated partial twisted zeta functions at $z=0$ and applying algebraic methods inspired by the strategies of Bir\'o, we derive explicit criteria under which the class number $h(D)$ is strictly greater than $1$. Our work contributes to the long-standing mathematical tradition that aims to solve the "class number one problem" for explicit families of real quadratic fields.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Bernardini

item.title: Consecutive moderate gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
item.description: arXiv:2412.15481v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $0<\gamma_1\leq \gamma_2 \leq \cdots $ denote the ordinates of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with positive imaginary parts. For $c>0$ fixed (but possibly small), $T$ large, and $\gamma_n\leq T$, we call a gap $\gamma_{n+1}-\gamma_n$ between consecutive ordinates ``moderate'' if $\gamma_{n+1}-\gamma_n \geq 2\pi c/\log T$. We investigate whether infinitely often there exists $r$ consecutive moderate gaps between ordinates $\gamma_{n+1}-\gamma_n, \gamma_{n+2}-\gamma_{n+1}, \ldots , \gamma_{n+r}- \gamma_{n+r-1}$.
item.dc:creator: Steven M. Gonek, Anurag Sahay

item.title: An Effective Version of Kronecker's Theorem on the Splitting of Polynomials and the $p$-Curvature Conjecture for Order One Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2510.00892v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an effective version of Kronecker's Theorem on the splitting of polynomials, based on asymptotic arguments proposed by the Chudnovsky brothers, coming from Hermite-Pad\'e approximation. In conjunction with Honda's proof of the $p$-curvature conjecture for order one equations with polynomial coefficients we use this to deduce an effective version of the Grothendieck $p$-curvature conjecture for order one equations. More precisely, we bound the number of primes for which the $p$-curvature of a given differential equation has to vanish in terms of the height and the degree of the coefficients, in order to conclude it has a non-zero algebraic solution. Using this approach, we describe an algorithm that decides algebraicity of solutions of differential equation of order one using $p$-curvatures, and report on an implementation in SageMath.
item.dc:creator: Florian F\"urnsinn, Lucas Pannier

item.title: Linear relations among radicals
item.description: arXiv:2511.02498v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a field, fix an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$, and let $G$ be a subgroup of $\overline{K}^\times$. We are able to give a closed formula for the ratio between the degree $[K(G):K]$ and the index $|GK^\times:K^\times|$, provided that the latter is finite. Our formula explains all the $K$-linear relations among radicals, which (beyond the ones stemming from the multiplicative group $GK^\times/K^\times$) are generated by relations among roots of unity and single radicals. Our work builds on results by Rybowicz, which in turn are based on work by Kneser and Schinzel.
item.dc:creator: Antonella Perucca

item.title: Topological flatness of orthogonal spin local models
item.description: arXiv:2512.16646v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $F$ be a complete discretely valued field with residue field of characteristic $p$. For any parahoric level structure of the split even orthogonal similitude group $\operatorname{GO}_{2n}$ over $F$, we prove a preliminary form of the Pappas-Rapoport flatness conjecture: the associated spin local model is topologically flat.
item.dc:creator: Jie Yang

item.title: Effective Joint Equidistribution of Subspaces of Bounded Height in Rigid Adelic Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.30608v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove effective joint equidistribution for subspaces of fixed dimension in a fixed rigid adelic space over a number field. The joint distribution records the rescaled height, the archimedean position, and the shapes of the subspace and its quotient. More generally, we obtain counting estimates for regions in which the height bound may depend on the position and both shapes. Under a H\"older-type bound for the measure of boundary layers, the estimates have explicit power-saving error terms. We apply these results to counting problems involving slopes, freeness, and semistability, and to Diophantine approximation with prescribed shapes.
item.dc:creator: Ruida Di

item.title: On Boston's Unramified Conjecture for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ and McLeman's $(3,3)$-Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.37252v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $A$ be a complete Noetherian commutative local ring with finite residue field of characteristic $p$. Let $G_{\mathbf{Q}}$ be the absolute Galois group of the rational number field and fix an inertia subgroup $I_p\subset G_{\mathbf{Q}}$ at $p$. We prove that every continuous odd representation $\rho:G_{\mathbf{Q}}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(A)$, unramified outside finitely many primes and with finite $\rho(I_p)$, has finite image if $p>3$ or $A$ has positive characteristic. For $p=3$, the conclusion also holds when the local representation at $3$ is reducible, or the local residual semisimplification has no mod-$3$ cyclotomic self-twist. In particular, this proves the two-dimensional odd case of Boston's unramified Fontaine--Mazur conjecture over $\mathbf{Q}$ for every odd $p$. Furthermore, we deduce finiteness results for conjugate self-dual representations of pro-$p$ Galois groups over imaginary quadratic fields under a ramification condition, and for representations of their unramified pro-$p$ groups of generator rank at most two. As an application, we resolve the sufficiency direction of McLeman's $(3,3)$-conjecture on $p$-class field towers for $p>3$. Namely, we prove that if $K$ is an imaginary quadratic field with $p$-class rank two and the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(K_{\varnothing}(p)/K)$ of the maximal unramified $p$-extension of $K$ has Zassenhaus type $(3,3)$, then the $p$-class field tower of $K$ is finite. For $p=3$, we also rule out infinite towers for ten of the thirteen fourth Zassenhaus quotients classified by Ahlqvist and Pink.
item.dc:creator: Yufan Luo

item.title: Semi-stable models, local heights and quadratic Chabauty for $X_0(N)^*$
item.description: arXiv:2609.40207v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quadratic Chabauty computations for $X_0(N)^*$ are complicated by local height contributions at primes of bad reduction. For squarefree $N$, we explain a strategy for constructing a global $p$-adic height for which all the contributions at the primes of bad reduction vanish. As our first main result, we show that such a $p$-adic height exists for all squarefree levels $N>714$. In order to do this, we first give an explicit description of the minimal regular model of $X_0(N)^*$ at primes of bad reduction, and show this model is semi-stable. Each component of this model gives rise to a linear condition which ensures that the contribution at that component vanishes. Using embeddings of quadratic orders into quaternion algebras, we obtain an upper bound for the number of these conditions; when the genus of $X_0(N)^*$ is greater than one more than this bound, there is enough freedom to choose a suitable correspondence, simplifying quadratic Chabauty computations. As an application, we determine the rational points on several curves $X_0(N)^*$ for which this was not done before.
item.dc:creator: Nikola Ad\v{z}aga, Maarten Derickx, Timo Keller

item.title: Pellarin's Identity, Carlitz Period, and Anderson Generating Functions over Arbitrary Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.03134v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish three results for a rank-one Drinfeld module over the coefficient ring of a smooth, projective, geometrically connected curve over $ \mathbb F_q$, with a closed point at infinity of arbitrary degree. First, a Tate-algebra unit exists in the module of special functions precisely when this module is free of rank one, that is, when the period lattice is isomorphic to the module of regular differentials; this proves the Gazda--Maurischat conjecture. Second, under the unit-anchor normalization for an isogeny to a principal-period target, a strictly normalized shtuka product and one characteristic residue give the fundamental period; the same defect equation gives the logarithm residue formula. Third, finite \'{e}tale torsion traces over the field of definition identify the first Frobenius twist of the normalized shtuka differential and express Pellarin's $ \mathcal L(1)$-series at a fundamental period. The source period lattice need not be free.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu

item.title: Riemann functions for almost primes and their counting errors
item.description: arXiv:2610.11024v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The real-axis jump of the prime-zeta function gives an integral form of Gram's series for Riemann's $R$-function. Applying the same operation to the almost-prime Dirichlet series defines functions $R_k$, with $R_1=R$. We prove absolute convergence, recover the classical fixed-order Selberg-Delange expansion, and identify the complementary Perron contribution to the exact count. A convergent incomplete-gamma endpoint expansion, together with the remaining lower cut, gives an exact representation of $R_k$, with explicit formulas for ranks one through four and a coefficient recurrence for every fixed rank. We then study the errors $R_k-N_k$. Under the Riemann hypothesis, their normalized mean-square zero spectra retain multiplicities; with simple zeros, the leading oscillations agree for every fixed $k$. An additional weighted logarithmic-gap moment gives a second-order spectrum and a positive constant in the $(\log\log X)^{-2}$ mean-square cancellation rate for consecutive values of $k$. The global spectral passages are justified by a uniform finite contour and a Gaussian-Laplace block estimate.
item.dc:creator: Martin Belton

item.title: Local Tate duality for syntomic cohomology in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.21622v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p>0$. We show that syntomic cohomology over $k$, with coefficients, and defined using Dodd's theory of $F$-gauges, satisfies local Tate duality. We also prove that syntomic cohomology over the ring of integers of $k$, again with coefficients, is Lagrangian with respect to the duality pairing. Finally, we show that, for $p>2$, these results recover Shatz's duality and Milne's orthogonality results for the cohomology of finite flat group schemes of $p$-power order over $k$.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Lazda

item.title: Joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function with arbitrary real shift parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.41600v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function for shifts $\zeta(s+id_j\tau)$ with arbitrary nonzero real parameters $d_j$ whose absolute values are pairwise distinct, and show that these conditions are optimal. As a consequence, we establish generalized strong recurrence for every finite family of nonzero real parameters, meaning that the corresponding shifts of the Riemann zeta-function simultaneously approximate each other. The only cases for which generalized strong recurrence remains unproved are those involving both zero and nonzero shift parameters, for which it is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis. Our proof combines Emsalem's generalization of the six exponentials theorem with a generalization of Pecherskii's rearrangement theorem that may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: {\L}ukasz Pa\'nkowski

item.title: Explicit bounds for the number of solutions to Roth-type inequalities over adelic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.06973v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we provide an upper bound on the number of a special system of Roth-type Diophantine inequalities over proper adelic curves. By refining the technique from previous work, we successfully eliminate the large-height restriction on the solutions. Furthermore, the constraints on the parameters within the inequality are further relaxed. We also give a constructive quantitative generalization of the Vojta-Dolce-Zucconi system, replacing compactness-based extraction by a discrete pigeonhole argument and a finite grid partition, so that the resulting bound has explicit dependence on the relevant parameters.
item.dc:creator: YuXi Li, GuanHeng Zhao

item.title: Symmetric compatibility of theta structures, with applications to change of level and isogenies
item.description: arXiv:2504.21058v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $m,n,d >1$ be integers such that $n=md$ and let $(B, \mathscr{M}, \Theta\_{\mathscr{M}})$ be a marked abelian variety of level $m$ over a field of odd characteristic. We study the theta structures of level $n$ for $\mathscr{M}^d$, and the theta structures on the abelian varieties $d$-isogenous to $B$, which are compatible with $\Theta\_{\mathscr{M}}$. When $d$ is odd and coprime to $m$, they correspond to the isotropic subgroups of $B[n]$, and this correspondence underlies the known algorithms in theta coordinates. In general, this is no longer true. We introduce the notion of symmetric compatibility of a torsion point with a symmetric level subgroup, and we show that a subgroup of $B[n]$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^g$ comes from a compatible theta structure if and only if it is isotropic and all its points are symmetric compatible. We extend to every $d$ Mumford's notion of compatible pairs of theta structures, defined by Mumford for $d=2$, and prove that it is equivalent to our notion, which can be tested on theta coordinates; we also describe exactly the remaining ambiguity, which explains the sign choices met when the duplication formula is used to change the level. As applications, we obtain change of level and isogeny algorithms without assuming that $d$ is odd and coprime to $m$, using $O(n^{3g} \log(d))$ and $O(n^{2g} \log(d))$ operations in the base field respectively. In particular, they give change of level algorithms for even $d$, and $2$-isogenies in level $4$ theta coordinates with an explicit control of the theta structure of the codomain.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Dequay (IRMAR), David Lubicz (DGA.MI, IRMAR)

item.title: A Dynamical Fekete-Szeg\H{o} Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2603.01684v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a compact set, symmetric with respect to the real axis and regular for the Dirichlet problem. A classical theorem of Fekete and Szeg\H{o} asserts that if $cap(E)\ge 1$ then every neighbourhood of $E$ contains infinitely many complete sets of conjugate algebraic integers. We prove a dynamical strengthening: $cap(E)\ge1$ if and only if every neighbourhood of the polynomially convex hull $Pc(E)$ contains filled Julia sets of monic integral polynomials of arbitrarily large degree. When $cap(E)=1$, we show that the minimal polynomials $P_n$ of distinct algebraic integers whose entire Galois orbits approach $E$ have filled Julia sets $K_{P_n}$ converging to $Pc(E)$ in the Klimek metric, and Brolin measures converging to the equilibrium measure $\mu_E$. The key step is that algebraic numbers of small Rumely height $h_E$ have minimal polynomials that are asymptotically minimal on $E$. As an arithmetic application, we show that the Call--Silverman canonical heights $\hat{h}_{P_n}$ converge to $h_E$ uniformly on $\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$.
item.dc:creator: Turgay Bayraktar, Melike Efe

item.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
item.description: arXiv:2607.23453v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. All the proofs in this paper have been formalized in Lean. The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha)$, the {\em isosceles-$\beta$} shape, in which $3\alpha+2\beta = \pi$ and $\alpha$ is not a rational multiple of $\pi$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree. The shape $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha+\beta)$ (where $3\alpha + 3\beta = \pi$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.
item.dc:creator: Michael Beeson, Grigore Ro\c{s}u

item.title: Special Loci in the Moduli of Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.08382v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce new techniques to study mixed-characteristic special loci in moduli spaces and give several applications, focusing in particular on the moduli space $\mathsf{M}_g$ of curves. These applications include Zariski density results for split Jacobians, non-density results for supersingular loci, and lifting results for algebraic cycles, all under appropriate numerical conditions. Our methods generalize to more-or-less arbitrary moduli spaces mapping to Hodge-type Shimura varieties (and even some settings beyond the Shimura case), and relate to questions raised by Oort and de Jong.
item.dc:creator: David Urbanik, Ziquan Yang

item.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.38386v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14,639,440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.
